mechanism_narrative: Transit-station footfall is recovering monotonically (-46.4 to -26.1 over four weeks) and retail trips are heavily transit-dependent, so continued transit normalization mechanically lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks above its trailing four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose +20.3 points across the four weekly means
failure_condition: If the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is at or below the trailing 28-day mean while TRANSIT continues to improve, the transit-led recovery channel is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has decayed from +5.1 to +1.4, showing households exhausting the stay-home margin; once the weekly mean drops below +2.0 points, discretionary out-of-home trips reallocate to retail venues and lift RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL weekly mean falls below +2.0 percent-change points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 5.1 to 1.4 across the four weekly means
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL prints below +2.0 for two consecutive weeks and RETAIL_REC's 28-day mean is flat or lower than the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: Retail recovery requires both workplace and transit re-engagement because office-adjacent and trip-chained purchases dominate; only the joint rise of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT produces a repaired retail catchment, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve by at least 2.0 points week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved -42.4 to -25.6 and TRANSIT -46.4 to -26.1 in lockstep
failure_condition: Weeks in which WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve by 2.0+ points are followed by a lower 28-day RETAIL_REC mean than weeks in which only one improves.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS prints above +50 in three of four weeks, indicating a durable outdoor-substitution regime in which discretionary leisure time and spend are diverted to green space rather than commercial venues, capping RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean exceeds +50.0 percent-change points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS reached 54.1 and 65.0 in the four-week window
failure_condition: If weeks with PARKS above +50 are followed by a higher 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC than weeks with PARKS below +50, outdoor substitution is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Grocery-and-pharmacy visits are converging toward baseline (-24.4 to -9.4), marking the unwinding of precautionary stockpiling; as routine provisioning normalizes, freed shopping trips spill into retail-and-recreation categories over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved 15.0 points across the four weekly means
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM continues converging to baseline for four more weeks while the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is no higher than the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: Workplace mobility remains deeply suppressed at -25.6, consistent with standing work-from-home directives; if WORKPLACES fails to gain at least 2.0 points in a given week, office-adjacent retail demand stalls and drags RETAIL_REC lower over the following week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week gain is below 2.0 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly gains decelerated to 2.0 points in the final week
failure_condition: Weeks with WORKPLACES gains below 2.0 points are followed by RETAIL_REC increases of equal or greater size than weeks with gains above 2.0 points.

mechanism_narrative: Transit restoration only converts into retail footfall when outdoor competition is bounded: with TRANSIT up at least 15 points and PARKS held under +70, mall and restaurant trips win the time-allocation contest, raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves at least 15 points versus four weeks earlier while PARKS stays below +70.0
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT gained 20.3 points while PARKS peaked at 65.0
regime_hint: transit-led reopening with bounded outdoor substitution
failure_condition: Joint observations of TRANSIT +15 points and PARKS below +70 are followed by a 28-day RETAIL_REC mean lower than the trailing mean.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September marks the end of peak outdoor season; the PARKS series at 65.0 is the seasonal high, and as daylight and temperatures fall, outdoor leisure hours shift indoors into retail-and-recreation venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean begins a sustained decline of 5 or more points from its four-week high of 65.0
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS oscillated 54.1, 29.9, 55.0, 65.0 while RETAIL_REC rose steadily 31.5 points
regime_hint: seasonal transition out of peak outdoor season
failure_condition: PARKS declines from its 65.0 high across the next four weeks and the 28-day RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the trailing 28-day mean.
